occurrences.source_excerpt:
Typical Human Cell
• Cell theory
• A cell is the structural and functional unit of life. All living organisms are composed of cells
• Human is multicellular organism
• Human body is composed of many cells
• Over 200 different types of human cells
• Types differ in size, shape, and subcellular components; these differences lead to differences in functions

source_pages.document_title: Lecture 2 - Human Cells, Basic Tissues, and Organs (July 2026)

occurrences.source_excerpt:
Cell Organelles in a Typical Human Cell
• Plasma membrane (Cell membrane)
• Functions:
• Separating cytoplasm (intracellular materials) and tissue fluid (extracellular fluid)
• Controlling what enters and what leaves cell
• Chemicals:
• Consists of membrane lipids (Phospholipids and Cholesterols) that form a flexible lipid bilayer
• Specialized membrane proteins float through this fluid membrane
• Transporter proteins
• Channel proteins
• Receptor proteins

• Stacked and flattened membranous organelles

• Pack into vesicles to release outside cell
• Pack into vesicles to fuse with cell membrane
• Pack into lysosomes

occurrences.source_excerpt:
Primary Tissues in Human Body
• Epithelial tissue
• a sheet of cells that covers body surfaces or cavities
• Two main forms:
• Covering and lining epithelium: covering external and internal surfaces
• example: skin, lining of oral cavity
• Glandular epithelium: Secretory tissue in glands
• example: salivary glands
• Main functions:
• Protection of underlying parts
• Absorption
• Secretion
• Sensory reception

source_pages.document_title: Lecture 2 - Human Cells, Basic Tissues, and Organs (July 2026)

occurrences.source_excerpt:
Primary Tissues in Human Body
• Lining epithelium can be divided into 3 types based on their cell shape:
• Squamous epithelium
• E.g. epidermis of skin
• Columnar epithelium
• E.g. lining of digestive tract
• Cuboidal epithelium
• E.g. ducts of sweat glands
• All types allow constant loss and renewal of cells

• Transporter proteins
• Channel proteins
• Receptor proteins

• Modifies, sorts, and packages proteins and lipids received from rough ER

• Pack into lysosomes

• Responsible for most types of movement
• Muscle cells have proteins that bring about contraction
• Three types of muscle tissues:
• Skeletal muscle tissue
• Cardiac muscle tissue
• Smooth muscle tissue

• Tissue
• Group of cells that are similar in structure and perform common or related function
• Four basic tissue types:
• Epithelial tissue
• Connective tissue
• Muscle tissue
• Nervous tissue

occurrences.source_excerpt:
Primary Tissues in Human Body
• Nervous tissue
• Main component of organs in nervous system (brain, spinal cord, nerves)
• Generate and transmit electrical signals to control body functions
• Made up of two specialized cell types:
• Neurons: specialized nerve cells that generate and conduct nerve impulses
• Supporting cells that support, insulate, and protect neurons

occurrences.source_excerpt:
Cell Organelles in a Typical Human Cell
• Nucleus
• Largest organelle
• Contains the genetic information (Chromosomes) for synthesis of nearly all proteins
• Responds to signals to control the kinds and amounts of proteins to be produced
• Most cells are uninucleate (one nucleus)
• Skeletal muscle cells, some bone cells, and some liver cells are multinucleate (many nuclei)
• Mature red blood cells are anucleate (no nucleus)
